children: Odisha is going to have a silicon valley with 870-acre of land dedicated for the industry between Cuttack and Bhubaneswar, said Mohan Charan Majhi, Chief Minister of the State. Accordingly, the State has gotten investment proposals worth over ₹30,000 crore.

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of Semicon India 2026 on Friday, he said the Odisha government is also planning to offer around 20,000 jobs over the next few years through the semiconductor ecosystem, and that enough talents were already being trained for the same.

“Odisha has approved five semiconductor manufacturing projects with a cumulative investment of ₹10,899 crore, expected to generate over 4,500 direct jobs and more than 16,000 indirect employment opportunities,” said Majhi. “These projects cover a broad spectrum of the semiconductor value chain, including Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductors, advanced packaging, glass substrate packaging, memory module assembly and power electronics.”
These products have applications across critical sectors such as electric vehicles (EVs), railways, defence, and energy, among others, he said.

Companies like SiCSem and Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions have already committed to invest in Odisha. In addition, India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)-supported projects have attracted investments from RIR Power Electronics for SiC power devices, Sancode Technologies for advanced packaging and ASP Semicon for memory module OSAT operations, he added.

“In parallel, SiCSem Phase-II is exploring a combined SiC and GaN fab and packaging facility, and QuadQuantum is exploring to set up a raw material SiC wafers facility, further expanding Odisha’s presence in compound semiconductors,” Majhi said.

The State has also approved a National Industry Co-Development Hub on Integrated Power Electronics at IIT-Bhubaneswar under the Indian Design, Semiconductors, Packaging and Systems (IDSPS) programme. The total project of ₹452 crore will be jointly funded by the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, the State government, Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) and industry partners, he said.

On a query by businessline on whether Odisha was planning for any job reservations for the locals, in wake of very specific skills required for the semiconductor industry, Majhi said the State was already imparting skills training through various institutions. not only one institute, but we have got plenty of institutions,” he said.

title: Odisha to set up ‘Silicon Valley’ as part of ISM: CM Majhi
